_comment: Freeze-proof system-protection policy — single source of truth, consumed by BOTH configuration_system-protection.nix (builtins.fromJSON, boot-time enforcement) AND build.sh (_apply_daemon_caps, live enforcement before every nix build). Hardware: Surface Pro 8, 8 logical CPUs, 8GB RAM, NVMe (none scheduler), zram swap + disk hibernate swapfile. The machine froze 10x because nix builds (running inside nix-daemon, NOT the client) ballooned RAM and thrashed pages to the disk swapfile. The fix layers: (1) nix-daemon hard-capped with MemorySwapMax=0 so a runaway build OOM-kills a compile job instead of swap-thrashing; (2) the GUI session gets guaranteed unreclaimable RAM; (3) an UNTOUCHABLE ISLAND (reserved RAM + realtime CPU + realtime IO) hosts the killers (freeze-guard + earlyoom) and the mesh (sshd/rescue) so they can ALWAYS act even when everything else is starved; (4) systemd-oomd (PSI) + earlyoom (threshold) + freeze-guard (PSI active killer) = triple-layer defense.

nix_daemon._comment: Hard caps on nix-daemon.service — the ACTUAL build worker (cc1plus/rustc/ld run as its cgroup children). MemorySwapMax=0 = the build subtree can NEVER swap (not zram, not the disk swapfile) → the kernel OOM-kills one compile job instead of thrashing the disk → the desktop never freezes. cgroup v2 memory.max on the parent caps the whole subtree. Applied LIVE before every build by build.sh because 'nixos-rebuild switch' reloads unit files but does NOT re-apply resource control to the already-running daemon (this drift left the live daemon at 6G/4G-swap and caused the freezes).

gui_session._comment: user-1000.slice (the KDE Plasma desktop). MemoryMin = RAM the kernel is FORBIDDEN to reclaim, so the compositor (kwin/plasmashell) stays responsive under build pressure. MemorySwapMax=0 = desktop pages never thrash to the disk swapfile.

reservation._comment: THE UNTOUCHABLE ISLAND (user requirement: 'watchdog+mesh MUST HAVE ownership of a never-touched area of disk+memory+cpu to ALWAYS kill whatever overwhelms the system'). Hosts: freeze-guard, earlyoom, sshd, rescue-ssh (connectivity.slice). MemoryMin = guaranteed unreclaimable RAM. CPU = SCHED_FIFO realtime priority preempts ALL normal processes even at 100% load. IO = realtime ioprio class always gets the NVMe queue. OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 = NEVER killed. So the killers + remote rescue can always run, no matter what.

watchdog._comment: freeze-guard: an ACTIVE PSI killer running in the untouchable island. Every interval_sec it reads /proc/pressure/{memory,io} 'full avg10' (= % of the last 10s in which ALL tasks were stalled). If either exceeds its limit, it SIGKILLs the highest-RSS process matching prefer_kill (browsers/compilers), else the highest-RSS process not matching avoid_kill. This is the backstop layer beneath the cgroup caps + systemd-oomd. Tunable here; baked into the service script at build time (reproducible).

oomd._comment: systemd-oomd — PSI-aware proactive killer (kills before the kernel OOM does). enableUserSlices/SystemSlice/RootSlice set ManagedOOMMemoryPressure=kill on the standard slices. DefaultMemoryPressureLimit = % sustained memory pressure that triggers a kill; SwapUsedLimit = % of swap (zram) used that triggers a swap-based kill (very effective with swappiness=150).

sysctl._comment: Writeback + reclaim tuning. Lower dirty ratios flush dirty pages earlier and in smaller batches → no giant NVMe writeback burst that spikes iowait. vfs_cache_pressure<100 keeps dentry/inode cache longer → less metadata IO. min_free_kbytes/watermark keep a kernel reserve so allocation never stalls hard. swappiness 150 = prefer compressed zram over disk (zram is RAM-backed).

testers._comment: Run via the same data-driven runner pattern as test-session-checkpoint.sh. Each check proves one guarantee of the freeze-proof contract.
